name: integrations
title: Integrations
summary: Claude Code and Codex get the official GitHub, Context7, and Convex plugins, and Claude can hand work to Codex.
day: Agents read and change your GitHub issues and pull requests, look up current library docs before they write code, and inspect your Convex deployments. With both AI plans, Claude hands a task or a review to Codex.
cost: Each plugin signs in once on each machine, and hedge doctor says how: a GitHub token for Claude, Context7 through its own sign-in or an API key, and Convex through its CLI. Codex's GitHub and Convex plugins use your ChatGPT sign-in. Convex starts off.
risk: The plugins act with the accounts you sign in with. Hedge removes only plugins that it installed, and keeps a plugin you turn off in your settings off.

workflows.name: GitHub
workflows.sentence: Agents read and change issues and pull requests through GitHub's official plugin.

workflows.name: Context7
workflows.sentence: Agents look up current library documentation through Context7.

workflows.name: Convex
workflows.sentence: Agents get Convex guidance and inspect the deployment of the project they work in.

workflows.name: Codex from Claude
workflows.sentence: Claude Code hands a task, a diagnosis, or a review to Codex through OpenAI's Codex plugin.

run: command -v claude >/dev/null || exit 1; out=$(claude mcp get plugin:github:github 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Status: .*Connected' && exit 0; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE '^ *Issue: HTTP 40[01]([^0-9]|$)' && exit 4; exit 1
checks.say: Hedge cannot check whether Claude's GitHub plugin reaches GitHub, because Claude Code does not run here.
checks.todo: Claude's GitHub plugin cannot reach GitHub. It reads a token from GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment that starts Claude Code. Create a fine-grained, read-only token on GitHub for the repositories you work in, export it in your shell profile, and start a new shell. You can export "$(gh auth token)" instead, but that puts your broad gh token into the environment of every agent you start. This check runs in hedge doctor's shell; an app that starts Claude Code with its own environment, such as T3 Code, needs the token there too. Hedge never stores the token.

run: command -v claude >/dev/null || exit 1; out=$(claude mcp get plugin:context7:context7 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Status: .*Connected' && exit 0; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE 'Status: .*Needs authentication' && exit 4; exit 1
checks.say: Hedge cannot check whether Claude's Context7 plugin is signed in, because Claude Code does not run here.
checks.todo: Claude's Context7 plugin is not signed in. In Claude Code, run /mcp, choose plugin:context7:context7, and authenticate.

run: [ -z "$CONTEXT7_API_KEY" ] || exit 0; command -v codex >/dev/null || exit 1; out=$(codex mcp list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; row=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep '^context7 ' | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//'); case "$row" in *' OAuth') exit 0 ;; *' Not logged in') exit 4 ;; esac; exit 1
checks.say: Hedge cannot check whether Codex reaches Context7, because Codex does not run here.
checks.todo: Codex cannot reach Context7. Run codex mcp login context7, or export CONTEXT7_API_KEY in your shell profile: Codex sends it to Context7 as a header and Hedge never writes it into config.toml.

checks.say: Hedge cannot check whether Convex is signed in on this machine.
checks.todo: Convex is not signed in on this machine. In a Convex project, run npx convex login. Each project then picks its own deployment, and agents should never point at a production deployment by default.
